content: Firestore 'test mode' rules allow read, write: if true (world open for 30 days, then requests are denied). The mode only differs by the default ruleset, so an app can ship to production with a fully open database. Firebase docs 'Fix insecure rules' warns that auth != null means ANY logged-in user has access to the whole database. The server Admin SDK bypasses rules entirely. Community reports (vibeappscanner, rootcrak, penetrify) confirm thousands of apps ship with allow read, write: if true. Correct posture: default-deny, explicit per-collection match blocks, validate field shapes, and use the rules simulator plus rules unit tests.
